newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on weak exports, technicals.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on weak exports, technicals.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower on Monday, pressured by the lowest weekly export inspections figure since 1982 and bearish technical indicators, traders said.

USDA on Monday pegged export inspections for the week ended December 26 at 4.5 million bushels, down from 13.5 million the previous week and the lowest level since 1982 when USDA began keeping computerized records.
"The bottom line is we're not seeing any significant upturn in demand, and (farmer selling) appears to be picking up," one trader said.
"Until we find enough demand to gobble up this supply, there isn't much hope," he added.
Traders noted key support at $4.02-1/2 a bushel on March was broken early and the market dipped to a low of $3.98.
Wheat closed down seven to three cents a bushel with March off seven at $3.98-1/4.
